title: P6 ScheduleOptions Release 26 Field Disposition
reference_version: Oracle Primavera P6 EPPM REST API Release 26
rule: Every current Release 26 ScheduleOptions REST field must have an explicit disposition. Metadata fields are classified separately from calculation-core options. Historical Integration API-only extensions are not silently treated as current REST fields. A typed internal representation does not certify lossless interchange-to-domain mapping; PriorityList and ResourceList remain pending until explicit adapter and authoritative resource-leveling regression evidence exist.

open_mapping_gaps.reason: The Release 26 REST schema exposes PriorityList as a scalar string, while the Integration API contract exposes String[]. The REST encoding into ordered PriorityListItem entries, including sort-order representation/defaults, is not established by the cited REST schema; a source-backed adapter and round-trip/resource-leveling evidence remain outstanding.

The canonical Shared Core domain and snapshot path preserve ResourceList as an ordered tuple/JSON array, including resource IDs containing commas. The remaining gap is the external wire adapter: Release 26 REST exposes a scalar string while the Integration API exposes String[], and the cited REST schema does not establish a lossless encoding/escaping rule. Keep this field pending until a source-backed REST adapter and round-trip/resource-leveling evidence exist.

known_gaps.detail: Ten of the 13 documented P6 priority fields are mapped through the typed boundary/resolver: Activity ID, Activity Priority, Early Start, Early Finish, Late Start, Late Finish, Free Float, Remaining Duration, Project Planned Start, and Total Float. The code now has a distinct optional internal Activity.original_duration value, but the documented PriorityList field is Original/Planned Duration; mapping that external field is deliberately still blocked because the exact context-dependent source semantics and import/storage/interchange contract are not established. The ambiguous original_or_planned_duration alias is rejected rather than guessed. Planned Finish and Project Priority also remain unavailable end-to-end.
Current SortOrder enum supports ASCENDING and DESCENDING only; P6 hierarchy sort semantics are not represented.

Regression coverage targets numeric/alphabetic Activity ID ordering, ordered Total Float vs Activity Priority during backward rollback, CPM-derived Late Start/Late Finish and Free Float priorities, Remaining Duration from explicit activity data, and separate internal Original Duration data contrasted with planned duration. Project Planned Start is now represented in the leveling input and propagated to forward/backward priorities. Remaining acceptance must cover the documented Original/Planned Duration semantics and wire mapping, Planned Finish and Project Priority, broader mixed-field precedence across ten mapped and three unmapped P6 fields, all sort-direction/tie combinations, source-backed import/storage/interchange round-trip, project-level planned-start provenance, lossless REST/interchange -> ScheduleOptions -> Shared Core round-trip, and deterministic backward retry results.

priority_list_compatibility_audit.compatibility_rule: The open PR #1457 candidate currently maps ten of the thirteen documented P6 priority fields, including Project Planned Start. It stores Original Duration separately from Activity.duration, but intentionally rejects the documented original_or_planned_duration priority alias until its exact source semantics and interchange mapping are verified. Exact-head CI is queued/in progress after the latest model/test changes. Independent semantic review remains required. Do not claim full PriorityList parity while Original/Planned Duration, Planned Finish, Project Priority, Hierarchy sort, and source-backed import/storage/wire round-trip acceptance remain unresolved.
priority_list_compatibility_audit.source_version: P6 Professional User Guide Version 26; relevant online pages last published 2026-05-29

documented_rules.rule: Priority row order is precedence order: each row takes precedence over every row below it. Priority rows are used only when multiple activities compete for the same resource at the same time.

If multiple activities are ready for leveling, the leveler applies the configured priority rows. For Activity ID ordering, number-like values sort before alphabetic values and blanks; when no priority codes are configured, Activity ID is the default.

The documented priority table has 13 fields and supports ascending and descending; Hierarchy appears only for hierarchical fields. The current Shared Core boundary maps ten documented priority fields; Original/Planned Duration, Planned Finish, Project Priority and Hierarchy remain gaps. A separate internal Original Duration value does not by itself satisfy the documented Original/Planned Duration priority contract.

reviewed_paths.finding: The typed boundary accepts internal field identifiers planned_duration and original_duration separately and rejects original_or_planned_duration. This avoids an unverified alias but does not by itself implement the single documented Original/Planned Duration criterion.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Define the source-backed resolver for the documented combined criterion, then test each activity state and missing-source case through the public scheduling boundary and round-trip adapters.

reviewed_paths.finding: The scheduler enriches leveling inputs from scheduler-owned activity data: planned_duration is copied from Activity.duration, original_duration from Activity.original_duration, late dates and Free Float from the CPM pass, and Project Planned Start from the leveling input field.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Prove each value's authoritative source and persistence/import/export path. Project Planned Start is only safe once its project-level provenance is established; a populated field alone is not provenance evidence.

reviewed_paths.finding: The internal comparator can read planned_duration and original_duration independently, while Planned Finish and Project Priority are not represented by distinct values in the inspected leveling model. The sort enum represents ascending/descending only.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Do not count internal helper values as documented-field parity. Add distinct source-backed model fields for Planned Finish and Project Priority, plus a documented Hierarchy sort representation, before claiming complete priority coverage.

evidence_required: Versioned source rule defining when Original Duration versus Planned Duration supplies the priority value
Tests for not-started, in-progress, completed, and missing original-duration data where source semantics apply
REST/interchange/storage round-trip with no silent alias or value substitution
Authoritative planned-finish source in the project/activity model
Forward and backward priority tests including ascending, descending, and tied values
Authoritative project-priority source and cross-project semantics
Mixed-field precedence tests and persistence/round-trip evidence
Trace from authoritative project planned-start field through API/import and storage to both leveling directions
Fail-closed behavior when the source value is absent
Typed Hierarchy sort mode restricted to documented hierarchical fields
WBS/parent-child precedence tests, including stable ties and both leveling directions
Source-backed Release 26 REST encoding and escaping rules distinct from Integration API array schema
Lossless ordered round-trip tests for priority entries, sort directions/defaults, and resource IDs containing commas
ConstructionPM CI, Client Typecheck, PostgreSQL Integration, and PostgreSQL Sync State Integration confirmed on one exact final SHA
